posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
Why are you making a plugin to do something that's built into MV by default?
Even if you want to pull up the quit option from someplace other than the menu, all you have to do is push Scene_GameEnd and all the code is already written for you.
(Personal opinion: I hate those confirmation dialogues. In 30-some years of playing video games, I have tried to quit by accident zero times. There's no reason to ask me again. How often do you accidentally quit, that you think it's a good idea?
)

posts.author: utunnels
posts.body:
Well when they make you a habit to click confirm for everything, a confirm dialogue won't prevent your from making mistakes.
But I don't think people usually bother to quit the game via the menu, so if someone see the dialogue there is a higher chance they click it by mistake.
As for me, I just press F5 or Alt+F4 or click the X button.

Unless you and these people are primarily playing RPG Maker games, many-to-most professional games have disabled Alt+F4 and you have to quit via the menu (or pulling up the task manager for some reason). I suspect a significant portion of the gaming populace isn't even knowledgeable about that Windows shortcut.
Not to mention it would bypass and screw with the "save and quit" that most games do.

My advice as a coder and teacher - it's going to be very difficult to progress that way. I strongly suggest you take some time to do a JavaScript tutorial/course. It won't have anything strictly to do with RPG Maker in the beginning, but you'll learn and understand what you're doing in a structured fashion with a logical progression of knowledge.
When you're done, everything you read in the code should
mean
something, such that you can look at MV's code and follow the flow of function calls to know what's happening.
There are lots of options if you Google it, I like the w3schools tutorial, starting with the Statements chapter.
